**Duct-Tape DOOM is now DERP, the DOOM Engine Remaster Project.** Same
project, new name, new repository address (the old one redirects). The
downloads are now `DERP-mac.zip`, `DERP-windows.zip` and `DERP-linux.tar.gz`.
The Mac app keeps its identity, so it still remembers your WAD folder.

**Heretic.** Raven's Heretic now runs on the same 3D renderer, lighting,
sound and music, worked out from the WAD like everything else. Pick a Heretic
WAD in the launcher, or put it in the `wads` folder, and it starts the
Heretic program that ships next to DOOM's. You need your own copy; both the
2025 `heretic.wad` and the original DOS `HERETIC.WAD` work. The effects are
tuned for its world: torches, chandeliers and serpent statues light their
rooms, stained glass glints and throws its colours on the floor, water is a
clear mirror, the Ice Grotto's floor is glassy, and the Torch item is a
flickering flame you carry instead of a flashlight. There is no window glass
and nothing to shoot out, and Heretic's own wind and waterfall sounds play
instead of DERP's made-up ones. Heretic is new and far less played than
DOOM; see `heretic/README.md` for what works and what doesn't yet.

**Embers.** Torches and fires shed a few one-pixel sparks that rise and cool
to dark red; in Heretic the game's wind carries them off. F4 → Embers.

**Glowing liquid edges.** Walls running straight into nukage, slime or lava
take the glowing strip the game paints on its own edge textures, like the
NUKE24 steps, instead of only the walls a mapper gave that texture.

**Shore ripples.** Liquids ripple along the walls they meet, drawn like the
splash rings: quick thin lines on water, slow broad ones on nukage and
slime, slow glowing ones on lava, a still dark line on blood.

**Big pools look like one body of liquid.** Far away and at grazing angles a
liquid's detail fades toward the animation's average colour, and the surface
drifts between calmer and rougher patches with long wave bands in the
reflection, so large pools stop reading as a tiled flat.
